sections.title: Akar and the infinitive
sections.content: *akar* means 'wants'. Like *szeretnék*, it goes with a verb in *-ni*: *Moziba akarok menni.* (I want to go to the cinema.) *Akar* is plainer than *szeretnék*: it says what you want, not what you would like, so keep *Szeretnél jönni?* for a polite invitation and use *Akarsz jönni?* with a close friend. The verb *tervez* ('plans') works the same way: *Sétálni tervezek.* (I plan to walk.) New words: *akar*, *tervez*.

items.english: I want to come to the party.
Do you want to go to the cinema?
We do not want to work.
What are you planning on Saturday?
I plan to go to the cinema.

sections.content: Put *nem* before *akar* to say you do not want to: *Nem akarok dolgozni.* The infinitive after it never changes.
